pr_title: feat: Support use of Duration in `to_string`, ergonomic/perf improvement, tz-aware Datetime bugfix
pr_body:
Closes #7174.

(Supersedes the now-closed #19663).

## New feature

* Support applying `dt.to_string()` to Duration cols, transforming them to an ISO8601 duration string (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Durations for details on this format).
* The `to_string` expression (for _all_ temporal dtypes) can now take the shortcut format string `"iso"`, which represents the dtype-specific ISO8601 format for the given column(s). Setting _no_ explicit format is equivalent to setting "iso", leading to some nice ergonomic improvements (detailed below).

_(**Note:** the ISO duration string conversion was validated against an established package that does the same conversion; created an ad-hoc parametric test against many tens of thousands of randomly-generated timedeltas, and everything tied-out. Included various edge-cases in the unit tests)._

## Ergonomics

* If you do _not_ supply a format string (previously not possible) or set it to`"iso"`, the associated dtype-specific ISO8601 format is used. This means that you can now make a single expression that will properly format _all_ temporal columns with their dtype-appropriate ISO format, rather than have to separately associate an explicit format string with each dtype.

  So, can now write...
  ```python
  df.select(cs.temporal().dt.to_string())
  ```
  ...instead of:
  ```python
  df.select(
    cs.datetime("ms").dt.to_string("%F %T.3f"),
    cs.datetime("us").dt.to_string("%F %T.6f"),
    cs.datetime("ns").dt.to_string("%F %T.9f"),
    cs.datetime("ms","*").dt.to_string("%F %T.3f%:z"),
    cs.datetime("us","*").dt.to_string("%F %T.6f%:z"),
    cs.datetime("ns","*").dt.to_string("%F %T.9f%:z"),
    cs.date("%F"),
    cs.time("ms").dt.to_string("%T.3f"),
    cs.time("us").dt.to_string("%T.6f"),
    cs.time("ns").dt.to_string("%T.9f"),
  )
  ```

## Performance

* Consolidated the four duration → string functions (and the new "iso" option) down to two, then optimised them using `itoa` conversions and `push/push_str` calls instead of relying on `write!` to do the integer transforms into the output string (~3x faster in local testing) 🚀 

## Bugfix

* Transforming a timezone-aware column to string (via `cast`) did not include the expected ISO timezone offset - spotted this with some new tests and fixed it.

## Examples

```python
from datetime import datetime, date, timedelta, time
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "td": [
        timedelta(days=-1, seconds=-42),
        timedelta(days=14, hours=-10, microseconds=1001),
        timedelta(seconds=0),
    ],
    "tm": [
        time(1, 2, 3, 456789),
        time(23, 59, 9, 101),
        time(0, 0, 0, 1),
    ],
    "dt": [
        date(1999, 3, 1),
        date(2020, 5, 3),
        date(2077, 7, 5),
    ],
    "dtm": [
        datetime(1980, 8, 10, 0, 10, 20),
        datetime(2010, 10, 20, 8, 25, 35),
        datetime(2040, 12, 30, 16, 40, 50),
    ],
}).with_columns(
    dtm_tz = pl.col("dtm").dt.replace_time_zone("Asia/Kathmandu")
)
```
Cast to dtype-specific ISO8601 string (the default, if no explicit format string given):
```python
df.select(pl.col("td","tm","dt").dt.to_string())
# shape: (3, 3)
# ┌───────────────────┬─────────────────┬────────────┐
# │ td                ┆ tm              ┆ dt         │
# │ ---               ┆ ---             ┆ ---        │
# │ str               ┆ str             ┆ str        │
# ╞═══════════════════╪═════════════════╪════════════╡
# │ -P1DT42.S         ┆ 01:02:03.456789 ┆ 1999-03-01 │
# │ P13DT14H0.001001S ┆ 23:59:09.000101 ┆ 2020-05-03 │
# │ PT0S              ┆ 00:00:00.000001 ┆ 2077-07-05 │
# └───────────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────┘

df.select(pl.col("dtm","dtm_tz").dt.to_string())
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
# │ dtm                        ┆ dtm_tz                           │
# │ ---                        ┆ ---                              │
# │ str                        ┆ str                              │
# ╞════════════════════════════╪══════════════════════════════════╡
# │ 1980-08-10 00:10:20.000000 ┆ 1980-08-10 00:10:20.000000+05:30 │
# │ 2010-10-20 08:25:35.000000 ┆ 2010-10-20 08:25:35.000000+05:45 │
# │ 2040-12-30 16:40:50.000000 ┆ 2040-12-30 16:40:50.000000+05:45 │
# └────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
```
Durations do not support strftime; instead `to_string` recognises only `"iso"` or `"polars"` as formats for durations - the latter results in the same string output that we display in the frame repr:
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "td1": [
            timedelta(days=-1),
            timedelta(days=0),
        ],
        "td2": [
            timedelta(weeks=4, days=-10, microseconds=999999),
            timedelta(weeks=20, days=20, hours=13, minutes=45, seconds=22, microseconds=134455),
        ],
    },
    schema={"td1": pl.Duration("ms"), "td2": pl.Duration("ns")},
)

df.select(
    pl.all().dt.to_string("iso").name.suffix("(iso)"),
    pl.all().dt.to_string("polars").name.suffix("(pl)"),
)
# shape: (2, 4)
# ┌──────────┬────────────────────────┬─────────┬───────────────────────────┐
# │ td1(iso) ┆ td2(iso)               ┆ td1(pl) ┆ td2(pl)                   │
# │ ---      ┆ ---                    ┆ ---     ┆ ---                       │
# │ str      ┆ str                    ┆ str     ┆ str                       │
# ╞══════════╪════════════════════════╪═════════╪═══════════════════════════╡
# │ -P1D     ┆ P18DT0.999999S         ┆ -1d     ┆ 18d 999999µs              │
# │ PT0S     ┆ P160DT13H45M22.134455S ┆ 0ms     ┆ 160d 13h 45m 22s 134455µs │
# └──────────┴────────────────────────┴─────────┴───────────────────────────┘
```

> i also notice that this does about 2-3 things together - is it possible to do any of them separately (like the tz-aware datetime bugfix)?

The bug is fixed as a side-effect of explicitly/centrally declaring the right ISO strings, and everything else is connected, so there isn't really anything to separate out 😅

issue_context.title: Improve `Duration => Utf8` cast; currently returns stringified physical (Int64) representation
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

At the moment casting `Duration` data to `Utf8` (string) isn't very useful; it gets converted to physical (i64) and is stringified from there; ideally we should probably re-use the same string conversion/formatting done on frame display, like so:

```python
from datetime import timedelta
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {'dur': [timedelta(days=1,seconds=123, microseconds=987654)]}
)
print(df)
# ┌───────────────────┐
# │ dur               │
# │ ---               │
# │ duration[μs]      │
# ╞═══════════════════╡
# │ 1d 2m 3s 987654µs │  << cast to string should produce this format?
# └───────────────────┘
```
**Current behaviour:** _(stringified i64; not useful)_
```python
df.select( pl.col('dur').cast(pl.Utf8) ).item()
# '86523987654'
```
**Preferred behaviour:** _(reuse display string-formatting for consistency)_
```python
df.select( pl.col('dur').cast(pl.Utf8) ).item()
# '1d 2m 3s 987654µ'
```
**Partial workaround:** _(requires inefficient call into python, and not quite the same format)_
```python
df.select( pl.col('dur').apply(str) ).item()
# '1 day, 0:02:03.987654'
```
comments:
Someone did ask about this on StackOverflow recently, they had issues when converting to Excel:

https://stackoverflow.com/a/78322388/

review_comments: this function's only ever called when the input dtype has already been validated, right?
Yup; that's really there to satisfy the match and prevent anyone calling it accidentally in the future, but it's not possible to hit it with the code as-written.

@alexander-beedie I think these formats are not ISO formats.
Doesn't the separator between the date and time have to be `T`?
Is it appropriate to use `iso` as an alias for something that is not an ISO format?

It seems that the true ISO format can be specified with `%+`.
https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html#fn7

It's not entirely straightforward - in this version each _component_ is ISO, with the components joined with a space. This was considered a valid ISO format itself until a subsequent standard amendment, but... it's a good point, and we should have an option for a strict ISO return _with_ the "T" separator. Think I'll add an "iso:strict" mode to handle this 🤔 (the format with a space is now technically known as RFC 3339, which is considered a subset of ISO 8601).

Thanks for your reply.

> RFC 3339, which is considered a subset of ISO 8601

It does not seem _subset_.
https://ijmacd.github.io/rfc3339-iso8601/

The space-separated format was a subset; the entire spec is not. ISO didn't help themselves by first allowing it and then later amending it (in 2019, I believe) 🥲

So, we have each component as ISO separated by a space ("iso") vs each component as ISO separated by "T" ("iso:strict"). Both can reasonably be named "iso", since we don't specify that the whole is "iso8601" specifically.

related, there's already

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/bd126d55d1e2996eea9dbe4be93c324c15646bd5/crates/polars-arrow/src/temporal_conversions.rs#L15-L30

should these constants be consolidated together somewhere?
Probably; do we have a place for such things that each crate can access? (I didn't add these consts, just moved them up to the top of the file for visibility :)
it might need doing separately to be fair
Yes, maybe we can move them to polars-utils in a follow up PR. That crate is available to all crates. Can have a `temporal` module.
